transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

The OE code on LG washing machines means 'Error Outlet' – the machine has tried to drain for about 13 minutes but couldn't empty the water. This is almost always caused by a blockage (like a coin, button, or heavy lint) in the pump filter or hose, rather than a broken part. Since you are worried about flooding, please do not open the filter door until the machine has been unplugged and any pressure in the small drain hose at the bottom left is released into a shallow tray or towels first. Let me know what you find inside.
I'm not unscrewing the filter myself, sorry, not after last time. Is there anything else I can check that doesn't involve that?

I understand your concern about flooding; that is a very valid reason to be cautious. Since we cannot access the filter, let's look for other simple causes of the OE code. The most common alternative is that the drain hose at the back of the machine is kinked or pushed too far into the waste pipe, preventing water from flowing out. Please check that the grey hose on the rear of the machine is straight and not blocked at the end where it enters your sink or standpipe.
Ok, the machine is pushed right back against the wall and the hose was squashed behind it. I've pulled it out and straightened it. Do I just try the spin again now?
Yes, please try that. The blockage may be cleared.
Tried the spin again. It drained a little slower than normal and then OE came up again. So what now?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Since the OE code has returned even after straightening the hose, the machine is still unable to clear the water. This means there is likely a blockage inside the pump itself (such as a coin or debris) or the pump motor has failed. And because accessing these internal components requires dismantling the appliance and dealing with standing water, this is now beyond safe owner repair. You will need to call an engineer to clear the blockage or check the drain pump.
